target.title: fix(feishu): WebSocket encryptKey SecretRefs are ignored at runtime
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu WebSocket users who explicitly configure `channels.feishu.encryptKey` as a SecretRef have that key ignored during runtime secret resolution, even though the same field works as a plain string.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Feishu account resolver now sends `encryptKey` through the existing SecretRef-aware path regardless of event transport. The Feishu runtime secret contract also treats explicitly configured top-level and account-level WebSocket `encryptKey` SecretRefs as active for enabled accounts.

This keeps `encryptKey` optional for WebSocket mode, preserves the existing webhook requirements, and leaves disabled-account secret resolution unchanged. The conflict resolution retains current `main`'s implicit-default-account secret-contract coverage while carrying forward the WebSocket-specific regressions.

## User Impact

Feishu WebSocket configurations can store an optional `encryptKey` in an environment-backed or runtime-resolved SecretRef and have the resolved value reach the Feishu SDK event dispatcher. Configurations that omit `encryptKey` continue to work as before.

## Evidence

- Ported onto current `main` and resolved the Feishu secret-contract test conflict while preserving both current-main regression cases.
- Complete affected regression files: 2 files passed, 28 tests passed.
- Near-real runtime proof used the production Feishu secret-contract collector, account resolver, and installed Feishu SDK `EventDispatcher`:

  ```text
  [info]: [ 'event-dispatch is ready' ]
  {"assignments":1,"connectionMode":"websocket","accountEncryptKey":"runtime-proof-key","dispatcherEncryptKey":"runtime-proof-key"}
  ```

- Changed TypeScript files pass `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint`.
- The exact synthetic pull-request merge preview passes the max-lines ratchet.
- Full extension typechecks were not rerun locally because the required attested cgroup resource envelope was unavailable; hosted CI remains the verification source for those protected lanes.
